question: Is rereading your notes a good way to prepare for a test?
keyIdea: You identified that familiar notes don't show what you can recall.
model: Not on its own. Familiar notes don't show what you can recall. Close your notes and test yourself over several days.
unsureKeyIdea: You may have the key idea. Compare with the model answer.
noMatch: No key idea or listed misconception found. Compare with the model answer.

misconceptions.label: Rereading builds memory
misconceptions.why: Familiarity can feel like knowing. Test your recall over several days.

misconceptions.label: Highlighting is studying
misconceptions.why: Marking words doesn't test recall. Close your notes and test yourself.

misconceptions.label: Cramming the night before works as well
misconceptions.idea: cramming works as well as spaced practice
misconceptions.why: Crammed material fades faster. Spread your self-tests over several days.

misconceptions.label: Some people only learn by watching
misconceptions.idea: some people can learn only by watching
misconceptions.why: A preference isn't a fixed learning style. Practise recalling what you watched.
